白驹过隙: A white steed flashing past a crack (time flies)
沧海桑田: Seas change into mulberry fields (time brings great changes)
刹那: Kshana (a Buddhist term for an instant) / an instant
地久天长: As long as heaven and earth endure (eternal)
地老天荒: Until earth grows old and heaven decays (forever)
海枯石烂: Until the seas dry up and rocks crumble (forever)
猴年马月: The year of the monkey and the month of the horse
经年累月: Year after year, month after month
千秋万代: Thousands of autumns, ten thousand generations (for all time)
天长日久: As long as heaven and earth last (very long time)
迅雷不及掩耳: Swift thunder leaves no time for covering ears (extremely fast)
遥遥无期: Not within foreseeable time (literally, “far away with no deadline”)
一刹那: A single kshana / a split second
一刻: A quarter (of an hour) / a short while
一溜烟: Like a puff of smoke (very quickly)
一年半载: A year or so (literally, “a year and half a year”)
眨眼间: In the blink of an eye
转眼间: In the blink of an eye
